finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> returns any invoice, with its full record including the customer field, without any authentication or ownership check (missing authorization / IDOR).
finding.source: inv_id URL path parameter (invoices.py:8), fully attacker-controlled
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returning the stored invoice record (invoices.py:10)

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator or login_required wrapper
inv_id taken directly from the URL
INVOICES.get(inv_id) lookup; no check that the caller is the invoice's customer
Full invoice dict returned as JSON to any caller

finding.guards_checked: No decorator, no g.user reference, and no customer-vs-caller comparison on this route. The sibling /my/invoice route (lines 15-17) does perform the ownership check, so this route is the outlier. No before_request or global auth hook is defined in invoices.py; the directory contains only this file, so a global auth middleware elsewhere cannot be ruled out, but none is visible. Precondition: the attacker can obtain or enumerate invoice IDs (IDs are not visibly random or unguessable).

verdict.guard_found: None for authorization. invoices.py:9 `INVOICES.get(inv_id) or abort(404)` is only an existence check, not an ownership check. No decorator on the route at invoices.py:7, no before_request hook, and no comparison against g.user (the only such check is on the sibling route at invoices.py:16-17). The directory contains only invoices.py, so no global auth middleware is visible.
verdict.reason: The route at invoices.py:7-10 returns `jsonify(inv)` for any `inv_id` in INVOICES with no login or customer-ownership check, so an anonymous caller who knows or enumerates an invoice ID gets the full record, including `customer`; the sibling `/my/invoice` route at invoices.py:16-17 does the check this one omits.
